title: Pearson Introduces AI-Powered Co-Writing Assistant for Clinical and Psychoeducational Evaluation Reports
summary: Pearson Introduces AI-Powered Co-Writing Assistant for Clinical and Psychoeducational Evaluation Reports | Pearson plc
body_markdown:
09 Sep 2026 published at 14:00 PM BST


*Secure assistant built into Pearson’s Q-global® and Q-Interactive® platforms aims to cut report-writing time in half while keeping professionals in full editorial control*


**HOBOKEN, N.J. — Sept. 9, 2026 —** Pearson has launched its AI-powered[Co-Writing Assistant](https://www.pearsonassessments.com/campaign/ai-cowriter.html) , a report-writing tool built specifically for professionals conducting psychological and educational evaluations. Integrated directly into Pearson's popular[Q-global](https://www.pearsonassessments.com/campaign/q-global-products.html) and[Q-interactive](https://www.pearsonassessments.com/campaign/prospecting-q-interactive.html) platforms, the Assistant supports data interpretation and reduces documentation burden by generating draft reports while keeping clinicians firmly in control.


**Why it matters:** Psychologists, counselors and other clinical professionals across schools, healthcare settings, and private practices are facing growing caseloads, often with[fewer resources](https://www.apa.org/monitor/2024/01/trends-more-school-psychologists-needed?) . Report writing is an essential part of the clinical evaluation process, but it can consume hours that might otherwise be spent working directly with students, patients, and families.


The Co-Writing Assistant aims to reduce time spent on report writing by 50% or more.


**How it works:** The Co-Writing Assistant is built directly into Pearson's Q-Global and Q-interactive platforms, which are already used in healthcare settings and ~60% of school districts across the U.S. It draws assessment data from Pearson's Q platforms, combines it with clinician-provided notes and documents, and generates draft narrative sections of psychological and educational evaluation reports. Clinicians remain fully responsible for reviewing and editing content, interpreting assessment results, and finalizing reports.


**What professionals are saying:** "Pearson is easier for colleagues to trust than other AI tools because the workflow stays inside an already-approved environment," commented one diagnostician in the Co-Writing Assistant pilot program. Time savings stood out for another who said, "I wrote an ID (intellectual disability) evaluation in probably 3.5 hours… it usually takes me 8 or more hours to write."


**Built for education and healthcare settings:** Unlike general-purpose AI tools, Pearson's Co-Writing Assistant draws on Pearson's own assessment intellectual property and uses assessment data and clinical frameworks within Pearson’s Q platforms to inform the development of the draft reports. It operates within Pearson's secure Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment, complies with applicable FERPA, HIPAA and HITECH requirements, and customer information is not shared with AI providers or used to train third-party AI models. All AI-related data handling follows Pearson's established privacy and security controls.


**Clay Richey, Managing Director for Clinical Assessment at Pearson, said,** "Creating something clinicians can trust was our first priority, and key to that trust is the secure environment Pearson provides for this kind of sensitive work. Our AI pulls from Pearson's incredible breadth of information, data, and knowledge and stays in our systems. Clinical professionals who have piloted the Co-Writing Assistant are using it with confidence and gaining hours of time with clients, and less with paperwork."


**Availability:** The Co-Writing Assistant is now available in the United States to Digital Assessment Library for Schools (DALS) and Digital Assessment Library for Health Care (DAL HC) subscription customers through Pearson's Q-global and Q-Interactive platforms.
